bluebook.interpretation: No significant STARLIKE enrichment on H-alpha flare dates.

poss.interpretation: Numerically negative exact-day coefficient, but not admitted as a solar-suppression effect because only two primary non-flare Palomar nights remain and the full nuisance model is high-dimensional relative to n=20.

technical_failure_audit.repair: Any NB2 fit with non-finite standard error, p-value or confidence interval is now explicitly classified MODEL_NONFINITE_INFERENCE_FAIL_CLOSED and excluded from admission rather than serialized as NaN.

identifiability_warnings: Primary POSS exact-day analysis has 18 flare versus only 2 non-flare nights.
The preregistered full nuisance design is high-dimensional for n=20, so asymptotic covariance may be fragile even when finite.
Six of seven POSS lag fits failed finite covariance inference and were correctly excluded; only lag 0 was finite.

The 360-minute sensitivity retains 26 Palomar nights with 23 flare and 3 non-flare and remains negative (IRR approximately 0.601, p approximately 0.023), but this does not solve the sparse-control problem.
The 1080-minute sensitivity has no event variation among the six retained Palomar nights and therefore cannot estimate a flare effect.
required_followup: Do not rescue the negative coefficient by tuning the patrol threshold or lag window.
If the negative POSS association is revisited, use a deliberately low-dimensional or exact randomization estimator frozen before rerun and report the leverage of each non-flare control night.
Prioritize independent event families with better exposed/unexposed balance, including complete sounding-rocket and high-altitude-balloon manifests.
Retain the official NOAA event+patrol denominator as the template for all future external-event calendars.
